summary: Marketed inward-investment prospect, not a project: Invest Highland (The Highland Council) lists 148 hectares at the Dounreay former nuclear site, Caithness, owned by the Nuclear Decommissioning Authority, as a potential hyperscale data centre location citing 'abundant clean and green power options' and subsea fibre links (Farice, potential AE-5). No developer, operator or planning application has been identified.
maturity_explanation: Agency marketing listing only. No named developer or operator, no planning record found on the Highland Council register or PlanIt for a data centre at Dounreay, and the site remains under active nuclear decommissioning by the NDA.
unknowns: Whether the NDA has agreed to, or is even aware of, the marketing of its land for data centre use, and what land could actually be released during decommissioning
What 'abundant clean and green power options' means in practice — no grid connection capacity, generation source or MW figure is stated
Actual status and landing arrangements of the cited Farice and prospective AE-5 subsea cable connectivity for a commercial data centre
Any developer or operator interest to date
